results.statement: For an actual original-coordinate cross matrix M and a selected family of physical 3x3 minors all containing one distinguished physical row h, if every other normalized selected row marginal is at most 1/2, then arbitrary same-side curvature is retained and the output has continuous density bounded by 5*2^(4/5)*sqrt(e)*||M[h,:]||_2^(1/5)*Z^(-1/5), where Z is the selected squared-determinant mass. The same coefficient gives the linear interval bound.

Combining the new one-anchor theorem with account03/B09 r32 pays a target-valid rank-two hub/star family whose physical hub leverage is exactly 1 and whose leaf same-side curvature has rank n-2: ||p||inf <22.507[n(1-2/n)^2]^(-1/5), hence <11.548 for n>=32.

required_source_application.application: Used the proved cap-one characteristic-function Lp lemma in both determinant estimates; separately applied Theorem H to F=2X0<c,Y>+<v1,Y>^2+<v2,Y>^2 to obtain ||p_F||inf<=4sqrt(2), with active spectrum {-1,1,1,1}.

partner_application.application: Used its actual Bernoulli compiler W>=(27/256)G_* and exact selected hub-pair factorization. For p0=(1,0), pb=(0,1/sqrt(r)), Walsh leaves and balanced high-rank D, every positive selected minor contains p0; the other hub marginal is 1/r and the moved-leaf marginal is <1/2, so the new theorem applies at hub leverage exactly one.

structural_regression: P=I_2 shows that hub leverage one need not have a diffuse conditional Pluecker partner; this refutes only an automatic Parseval-spread routing claim, not QFORM.
unresolved_implication: QFORM-HIGH-HUB-CONCENTRATED-PLUCKER-PAIR-OR-PAID-EXIT-v1: when a very-high-leverage hub has more than half of its conditional two-dimensional Pluecker mass on one physical partner row, force an already-paid physical-pair/zero-hub/ridge/grouped-cross/definite exit or prove a two-hub-plus-general-leaf-curvature smoothing theorem retaining the external third source direction.
